nvitk.stats.summaries¶

Per-group descriptive statistics for one measurement.

Description¶

The question “what is the mean flow per territory, and how variable is it?” comes up constantly, and answering it currently means exporting the whole frame and pivoting it in a spreadsheet. This module is that table: one row per group, the statistics a methods section actually reports, computed once and identically whether they are read on screen or written to Excel.

What is reported, and why¶

Both the parametric and the robust summaries are always produced rather than one being chosen for you: 4D-flow measurements are frequently skewed by a handful of bad segmentations, and a table that silently reported only the mean would hide exactly that.

nvitk.stats.summaries.OVERALL_LABEL = 'ALL'¶
nvitk.stats.summaries.summarize_by_group(frame: pandas.DataFrame, column: str, *, by: str | Sequence[str] = '', ci: float = 0.95, include_overall: bool = True, sort_by: str = 'group') → pandas.DataFrame¶

Descriptive statistics of column, one row per group of by.

Parameters:

  • by (str or sequence of str) – Grouping column(s). Several are combined into one label (Left_ICA | male) rather than a MultiIndex, so the sheet stays flat and readable. Empty summarises the column as a whole.

  • include_overall (bool) – Append an OVERALL_LABEL row over every group. Worth having in the same table — a per-territory mean is usually read against the whole-cohort one.

  • sort_by ({"group", "mean", "median", "n"}) – Row order. "group" sorts naturally, so g2 precedes g10.

Returns:

Columns as in SUMMARY_COLUMNS. frame.attrs carries column, by and ci so an exporter can label the sheet without being told again.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – When column or a grouping column is absent, or column holds nothing numeric.

nvitk.stats.summaries.summary_provenance(summary: pandas.DataFrame, *, dataset: str = '', n_rows_source: int | None = None) → pandas.DataFrame¶

Two-column record of what a summary describes, for the export’s second sheet.

A table of means with no note of which column, which grouping, which confidence level or how many rows it came from is unreconstructable a month later — including by its author.
